newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Sodra still holds off pulp price hike.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Sodra still holds off pulp price hike.

text.p: Sodra Cell, a unit Swedish non-traded forestry group Sodra, said on Tuesday it was too early to announce a price hike on pulp.
"We don't want to stand up for something that feels so uncertain," Sodra Cell's chief executive Tom Almgren told Reuters.
"There is a lot of activity on the U.S. market but that is not the case in Europe," he said.
Almgren mentioned uncertainty surrounding the fine paper market during the usually sluggish summer season.
U.S. pulp producers announced earlier this month that they would raise prices on softwood pulp by $50 per tonne to $630 as of July 1.
On Monday, Portuguese pulp group Portucel Industrial-Empresa Produtora de Celulose said it would raise prices on hardwood pulp by 40 ecus per tonne to 490 as of July 1.
Sodra Cell has said it wanted to wait for a possible price hike on hardwood pulp before raising its prices.
